title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's motivic Galois theory notes. The neighbouring pages in the scan are unrelated typescript on holomorphic ODEs (Bourbaki-style), so this sheet stands alone. The local categories it uses suggest the object is the category of supersingular elliptic curves (or supersingular rank-2 motives) over \bar F_p up to isogeny. I call it the 'Deuring category', because its endomorphism algebra is the quaternion algebra ramified exactly at p and infinity. The page studies this category through its adelic realization, place by place.

(1) Away from p. On A' = \prod_{\ell \neq p,\infty} Z_\ell, the realization category C_1^#(A') with fibre functor T' is taken to be the one attached to the gerbe of objects built from A'(1), i.e. the prime-to-p Tate modules. This depends on choosing an algebraic closure \bar F_p.

(2) At p. C(Z_p) is the category of F-crystals over \bar F_p, up to isomorphism, of rank 2 and slope 1/2, i.e. the Dieudonné modules of supersingular curves, together with the 'Tate Frobenius'.

(3) At infinity. C(R) is the category attached to a gerbe g'_\infty over R. Plausibly this is the gerbe of the Hamilton quaternions, or the Weil-group gerbe of R.

For each object C, comparing the global object with these local realizations gives a torsor T'(C) under
\Gamma' = A'^*/A'^{*2} \times (Z_p^*/Z_p^{*2} \times Z/2) \times R^*/R^{*2}.
The middle factor is just Q_p^*/Q_p^{*2}, units mod squares times valuation parity. So \Gamma' is the 'unramified-outside-p' part of \prod_v Q_v^*/Q_v^{*2}. These are typically determinant / reduced-norm classes mod squares, i.e. orientation or spinor data.

The group Z/2 of isomorphism classes of autoequivalences, generated by Frobenius f, acts on the torsor. Since its action on the structure group is trivial, it acts by translation through a homomorphism into \Gamma'. Its image is (p, (0,1), p): the global element p seen as an \ell-adic unit, then valuation 1 with trivial unit part at p, then p at infinity. The N.B. observes that p > 0 is a square in R, so the infinity component is trivial.

One then sets \Gamma = \Gamma'/f(\pm1) and T(C) = T'(C)/\pm1. This is a torsor under \Gamma, identified with T(\bar F_p) via the image of C, hence independent of C. Finally, let \Gamma_0 = A'^*/A'^{*2} \times Z_p^*/Z_p^{*2} \times R^*/R^{*2}, the units of the integral adèles mod squares, which Grothendieck labels H^1(A, F_2). Because f projects isomorphically onto the Z/2 factor, \Gamma' = \Gamma_0 \times f(\pm1), so \Gamma \cong \Gamma_0 canonically.

Purpose: a Hasse-principle / local-global analysis of the motivic gerbe of supersingular motives. It computes the adelic 'orientation' torsor and shows that the global Frobenius (the rational number p) cancels the valuation part at p. This is a quotient by a global element, like an idèle-class computation.
errors: For p = 2 (and in the \ell = 2 factor of A') units mod squares have order 4, not 2; the decomposition Q_p^*/Q_p^{*2} = Z_p^*/Z_p^{*2} x Z/2 still holds, but the explicit structure differs. The text is silent on this, harmless.
Calling \Gamma_0 'H^1(A, F_2)' is loose. Restricted-product adelic H^1(A, \mu_2) is \prod' Q_v^*/Q_v^{*2}, whereas \Gamma_0 is only the unit (integral) part, i.e. H^1 of the integral adèles.

Why the autoequivalence group is Z/2 generated by Frobenius (rather than Z) is not justified on the page. Presumably it uses the fact that the p^2-Frobenius equals \pm p on supersingular objects, so it is trivial up to isomorphism in the isogeny/torsor setting; this is a gap in the visible text.

ideas.what: Adelic description of the category of supersingular elliptic motives over \bar F_p via local realization categories: Tate modules away from p, slope-1/2 rank-2 F-crystals at p, a gerbe over R at infinity
ideas.modern_name: Local gerbes / pseudo-motivic (quasi-motivic) groupoid for supersingular motives; Deuring–Tate–Honda theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Langlands–Rapoport (1987, Shimuravarietäten und Gerben); Milne (1992-2003, motives over finite fields); Kottwitz (local gerbes); Deuring 1941 and Tate 1966 for the underlying facts
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's motivic Galois / Tannakian programme appears in Saavedra Rivano (1972) and Récoltes et Semailles in general terms; this adelic supersingular computation does not appear there

ideas.what: Torsor T'(C) under the product of local square classes, comparing a global object with its local realizations, and its quotient by the global Frobenius element p
ideas.modern_name: Hasse-principle comparison for gerbes; idèle-class-type quotient (global p acting diagonally on local square classes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Langlands–Rapoport / Kottwitz (Hasse principle for gerbes and Shimura varieties); Milne

ideas.what: Decomposition Q_p^*/Q_p^{*2} = Z_p^*/Z_p^{*2} x Z/2 and the splitting \Gamma' = \Gamma_0 x <f>
ideas.modern_name: Elementary local class field theory / square classes

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly models the motivic category of supersingular curves adelically. He uses a gerbe at infinity over R, F-crystals at p with the Tate Frobenius, and Tate modules at \ell. He then computes the comparison torsor and the effect of the global Frobenius. This is structurally the Langlands–Rapoport 'pseudo-motivic gerbe' philosophy with local gerbes at p and infinity, roughly 15+ years earlier. It is not credited to him.
missed.quote: la catégorie de Deuring C(Z_p) comme celle des F-cristaux sur \bar F_p (à iso près) qui sont de rang 2, pente 1/2 avec la Frobenius de Tate, et la catégorie C(Z_\infty)=C(R) comme associée à la gerbe g'_\infty
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents an early Grothendieck origin for the local-gerbe/adelic approach to motives over finite fields. That approach was later central in Langlands–Rapoport and Milne, and in the Kisin and Kisin–Madapusi–Shin work on the Langlands–Rapoport conjecture. It would refine the history and possibly suggest the explicit square-class torsor computation as a toy case.

missed.claim: The page computes a canonical \Gamma \cong \Gamma_0 torsor independent of C and stops ('donc ...'). The intended conclusion appears to be a triviality or obstruction statement for the motivic gerbe relative to its adelic realization. That conclusion is not on this page.
missed.quote: on trouve que \Gamma'=\Gamma_0\times f(\pm1), d'où \Gamma\simeq\Gamma_0 can, donc
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a worked toy example of a Hasse-principle computation for a motivic gerbe with nonabelian (quaternionic) bands. Such examples are rare in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The ingredients (Deuring, Tate, Dieudonné theory, square classes) are classical. What is notable is the unpublished adelic gerbe set-up: F-crystals at p, a real gerbe at infinity, and a Frobenius torsor computation. It anticipates the Langlands–Rapoport local-gerbe formalism and is absent from the record under Grothendieck's name. The handwriting is very hard to read, though, and the exact objects (e.g. the infinity gerbe) are uncertain, which tempers the score.
transcription_corrections: The header insertion reads approximately 'catégorie de Deuring-gerbe' (the 'gerbe' word is partly struck through).
'gerbe des variétés courbes de A'(1)' is doubtful. It is likely 'gerbe des ... de A'(1)' referring to lattices or Tate-module objects; the exact word is illegible.
The torsor is first written '\underline{Isom}(C)' (struck through) and replaced by '\mathcal{T}'(C)'.
The N.B. reads roughly 'Comme p \in R^{*2}, ... [struck: l'un des ... polarisations / quaternions] ... Pour C il y a un système transitif d'isomorphismes!'. Here 'R(C)' is probably 'Pour C'.

'Ce torseur est isomorphe uniquement' is more likely 'Ce torseur est isomorphe, i.e. canoniquement' (insertion: 'via l'image de C in \mathcal{T}(\bar F_p)'). The target is \mathcal{T}(\bar F_p), not \mathcal{T}(F_p).
'H^1(A, F_2)' is annotated 'adèles' underneath; the A is probably the adèle ring (bold A).
